title: console: field designer still offers an "Indexed" toggle for a key FieldSchema rejects by name — ticking it hard-blocks the save
body:
Measured on `@objectstack/console` **17.0.0 GA** in a real browser, downstream at objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1122 (GA close-out probe objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1154).

Filed here rather than in `objectstack` because the fix is in the console field designer (`metadata-admin` bundle) — and because both prior console-chrome cards from this family landed here (PR #3379, PR #4602), per the maintainer's file-at-destination ruling (objectstack-ai/objectstack#7167, 2026-08-10).

## The contradiction, both ends verified on GA

**The designer ships the control.** `dist/assets/metadata-admin-DqAvOmNf.js`, console 17.0.0 GA:

```js
label:c(`designer.field.indexed`),value:!!C.indexed,onCommit:e=>D({indexed:e||void 0}),disabled:o
```

`designer.field.indexed` is translated in the shipped locale bundles, so this is a fully finished, intentional-looking control.

**The spec refuses the key it writes.** Against `@objectstack/spec` 17.0.0 GA:

```
FieldSchema.safeParse({ name:'foo', label:'Foo', type:'text', indexed:true })
  → success = false, code = unrecognized_keys
  → "Unrecognized key(s) on this field: `indexed`.
     • never a FieldSchema key; a field-level index flag built no index (#2377).
       Declare the index in the object's `indexes[]`. …"

control — the identical field WITHOUT `indexed` → success = true
```

`FieldSchema` has no `index` / `indexed` key at all; the real surface is object-level `indexes: [{ name, fields, unique }]`, materialised by `SqlDriver.syncDeclaredIndexes`.

## Round trip in the browser — what an admin actually gets

Writable package created in Studio, one object, Data → Form · Layout → click a field → **Field properties**:

1. The **ADVANCED** section renders `Read-only`, `Hidden`, **`Indexed`**, `External ID`, `Track history`. `Indexed` is offered on a plain field, unchecked and fully enabled.
2. Tick it — `aria-checked` flips `false → true`.
3. **Save draft**:

```
PUT /api/v1/meta/object/probe_widget?mode=draft&package=com.probe.p1154
→ HTTP 422
{"error":"[invalid_metadata] object/probe_widget failed spec validation:
  fields.owner_id: Unrecognized key(s) on this field: `indexed`. …",
 "code":"INVALID_METADATA",
 "issues":[{"path":"fields.owner_id","message":"Unrecognized key(s) on this field: `indexed`. …"}]}
```

4. The draft does not save. Header stays `Unpublished draft`, sub-header flips to `Draft layout — your unsaved changes`, and the toggle **stays ticked**.

**The rejection is loud, not silent** — the console renders a red inline banner carrying the full spec guidance (#2377 / #4001 text included). That part is working as intended and is worth keeping.

## Why this is still a bug

The defect is not the error — it is that the designer offers a control whose value **can never be persisted**. The only reachable outcome of ticking `Indexed` is a hard-blocked save on a key the UI itself just wrote, and every subsequent save of that object stays blocked until the user finds and un-ticks it. The control promises an index nobody creates, which is exactly what #2377 removed the field-level flag for; the UI was not retired alongside it.

## Suggested fix

Retire the toggle from the field designer. If an index-authoring affordance is wanted in Studio, it belongs on the **object**, writing `indexes[]` — not on the field. Same treatment presumably applies to any sibling control writing a retired `FieldSchema` key; `External ID` sits right next to it and is worth checking in the same pass (not measured here).

Refs: objectstack-ai/objectstack#2377 (field-level flag removed), #4001 (silent-drop closed → loud rejection), #5248 (sibling `indexes[].type` / `indexes[].partial` removals).
Downstream: objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1122.
